Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

yourselves pronoun

also you yourselves, enjoy yourselves, look after yourselves

classical

Cic. Agr. 2.29.79: dēlūdī vōsmet ipsōs … patiēminī? (Lewis & Short, s.v. dēlūdō)

vōs, vōbīs (reflexive)

pronoun: the ordinary forms of vōs, used reflexively

yourselves (as object)

No separate reflexive; stressed, vōsmet or vōsmet ipsōs. English “enjoy yourselves” and “look after yourselves” need no reflexive in Latin: ut vōbīs suāviter sit; date operam ut valeātis.

Other words

  • ipsī, ipsae, ipsa — yourselves (for emphasis: you yourselves)

    pronoun, intensive (plural of ipse) · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 104: ut ea contrā vōsmet ipsōs facere videāminī (Lewis & Short, s.v. contrā) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Agrees with vōs as subject or as object, as with yourself.

Examples

  • dēlūdī vōsmet ipsōs diūtius ā tribūnō plēbis patiēminī?

    Will you let yourselves be fooled any longer by a tribune of the people?Cic. Agr. 2.29.79 (Lewis & Short)

  • ut ea contrā vōsmet ipsōs facere videāminī

    so that you seem to be doing it against yourselvesCic. Rosc. Am. 104 (Lewis & Short)

  • vōs rogō, amīcī, ut vōbīs suāviter sit

    I ask you, friends, to enjoy yourselves.Petr. 75.1

  • maximē autem date operam ut valeātis, sī nōs vultis valēre

    Above all, take good care of yourselves, if you want me to be well.Cic. Fam. 14.18.2

See also you, yourself, ourselves.
